 Interrupter clause to be invoked for gas prices in Nova Scotia, but not diesel
 Market conditions in the oil industry have been trending downward the past few days.
 Author of the article: By Willy Palov Published Nov 06, 2026 Last updated 17 hours ago 1 minute read The interrupter clause will go into effect for gas prices in Nova Scotia at 12:01 a.m. on Saturday. Photo by Postmedia Article content The interrupter clause will go into effect for gas prices in Nova Scotia at 12:01 a.m. on Saturday.

Activate your Online Access Now Article content The Nova Scotia Energy Board uses the mechanism to introduce a change outside the weekly regulated adjustment. All grades of gasoline will be included in the change, but the price of diesel is not affected.
 Article content Article content A news release from the board did not identify whether there will be an increase or decrease, but general market conditions in the oil industry have been trending toward lower prices the past few days.
 Article content Advertisement 1 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content The current price range of regular unleaded gasoline in Zone 1, which includes the Halifax Regional Municipality, is 171.7 to 174.7 cents per litre after a drop of 9.9 cents Friday. The interrupter was used Wednesday to lower the price of diesel by 13.3 cents per litre.
 Article content Regular unleaded gas rose to 204.1 cents per litre in Nova Scotia six weeks ago.
 Article content The release described the following process when determining price-setting:
 Article content “The benchmark price for gasoline is based on the average daily market price of refined gasoline traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange. That average price is then converted into Canadian dollars.
 Article content “The retail price paid at the pumps is the benchmark price with the following added: wholesale margin, retailer markup with added adjustment, cost of clean fuel regulations, transportation allowance, winter blending (when applicable) and taxes.”
